　クロには朔屋ほどの背丈であっても正面に立たれるとのしかかられるよう、クロにとって上から降ってくるものは叱り飛ばす声とか張り倒す手などがほとんどで、反射的に身が竦む、けれど朔屋は腰を屈めて少女と目線を合わせたのである。
lines.english:
He drew the towel hanging from his waist and approached. Kuro flinched again, looking anxiously along the passage in both directions. Did she see him as a dormitory supervisor harshly condemning her late hours? Her mouth trembled in search of excuses. Realizing she was too close to escape, she tried to make that cringing smile again—then it slackened in surprise.
Even a man of Sakuya's height seemed to loom when standing before her. Most things that descended on Kuro from above were scolding voices or hands that knocked her down. She shrank reflexively. But Sakuya had bent to meet the girl's eyes.

lines.japanese: 盆暗の朔屋にしては利け者の気転も、クロがいつも通りの哀れなクロに戻っていたから利いた事で、相手より優位と知ると人には自ずと余裕が生まれるからだが、それでもクロにはよく効いて、彼女の緊張は青年の狙い通りに解れる。船窓を閉めて、雨風を閉めだして。
lines.japaneseRuby: [R盆暗^ぼんくら]の朔屋にしては利け者の気転も、クロがいつも通りの哀れなクロに戻っていたから利いた事で、相手より優位と知ると人には自ずと余裕が生まれるからだが、それでもクロにはよく効いて、彼女の緊張は青年の狙い通りに解れる。船窓を閉めて、雨風を閉めだして。
lines.english: Unusual ingenuity for the dull Sakuya, made possible because Kuro had returned to her usual pitiable self. Knowing oneself superior naturally grants a little ease. Even so, it worked well on her. Her tension loosened as he intended. He closed the porthole, shutting out the wind and rain.

lines.japanese: しばらくは朔屋に頬や瞼[まぶた]を拭われるままに任せていたクロだったが、やがて、ぽつりと。
lines.english: For a while Kuro let him wipe her cheeks and eyelids. At last she spoke, quietly.

lines.japanese:
「……クロは。やっぱり……。
　駄目、なのかなあ……」
lines.english:
“…Is Kuro… no good,
after all…?”

lines.japanese: 「せっかくの、ずっと吹いてる嵐のところに来たのに……」
lines.english: “Even after coming all this way, to a place where there's always a storm…”

lines.japanese:
「あれで駄目なら、他の奴だって駄目だろ。
　ま今回は、多少は手こずったみたいだが」
lines.english:
“If that counts as no good, everyone else is no good too.
Well, you seemed to have a bit more trouble this time.”

lines.japanese:
駄目。だめ。ダメな奴。
　
　朔屋が何度耳にした評価だったろう。
　ただ朔屋の方は自分がそうと言われても当然の人間だと早々に開き直り、むしろ軽んじられる事に逆説的な気楽さを見出したものだ。常人には当然の努力も勤勉も、自分には続けられる甲斐性もないと、とある女の情夫になってはや一週間目に覚った自堕落男。
　だが朔屋はそうと開き直れてもクロには？　待望していた『止まない嵐』に我が身を置いてみたのに、願っていたような明晰な感覚が曇ってしまったクロには？
lines.japaneseRuby:
駄目。だめ。ダメな奴。
　
　朔屋が何度耳にした評価だったろう。
　ただ朔屋の方は自分がそうと言われても当然の人間だと早々に開き直り、むしろ軽んじられる事に逆説的な気楽さを見出したものだ。常人には当然の努力も勤勉も、自分には続けられる甲斐性もないと、とある女の[R情夫^ヒモ]になってはや一週間目に覚った自堕落男。
　だが朔屋はそうと開き直れてもクロには？　待望していた『止まない嵐』に我が身を置いてみたのに、願っていたような明晰な感覚が曇ってしまったクロには？
lines.english:
No good. No good. A no-good fellow.
How often had Sakuya heard that judgment? But he had quickly become defiant about being someone who deserved it. He even found a paradoxical ease in being looked down on. An idle man who, a mere week after becoming a woman's kept man, realized he wasn't capable of sustaining even the effort and diligence ordinary people took for granted.
Sakuya could shrug it off. But Kuro? Kuro, who had at last entered the ‘storm that never ends’ she longed for, only to find her hoped-for clarity clouded?

lines.japanese: クロの呟きは、怠惰の粘液に塗れた朔屋の心の芯にさえ、ずしりと重く響いたという。
lines.english: Her murmur landed heavily even at the core of Sakuya's heart, coated in the slime of idleness.

lines.japanese: 「朔屋さん、クロは怖いよ」
lines.english: “Mr. Sakuya, Kuro's scared.”

lines.japanese:
「おかしいの。クロがちゃんと船長になれないのが怖い。でも今は、ちょっと違う、
　それだけじゃない」
lines.english:
“It's strange. Kuro's scared of not being able to do the captain's job right. But now it's a little different.
That's not all.”

lines.japanese: 台風の目の中という事で、クロのスイッチは中途半端に入ったままであり、いつもよりはやや言も明瞭だが、船を指揮する状態には程遠い。
lines.english: In the storm's eye, Kuro's switch remained halfway on. Her words were a little clearer than usual, but far from the state in which she commanded the ship.

lines.japanese: 「クロはなんだか……この島が怖い」
lines.english: “Somehow… Kuro's scared of this island.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい……」
lines.english: “Hey, now…”

lines.japanese:
「せっかくの、ずっと探してた、
『止まない嵐』、なのに……」
lines.english:
“Even though it's the ‘storm that never ends,’
the one Kuro's been searching for all this time…”

lines.japanese: もう慰めの言葉も見当たらず、ただ機械的にクロの濡れ髪の水気をタオルに吸わせ続けるしかない朔屋、こんなやせっぽちの肢体に動く男心はないけれど、それでも一つ奮発して抱きしめてやるのはどうだろうと、クロの前に膝でにじった時───
lines.english: There were no words of comfort left. Sakuya could only keep mechanically soaking up the moisture in her hair with the towel. The scrawny girl held no attraction for him, but perhaps he ought to make the effort and give her a hug. He shuffled forward on his knees—

lines.japanese:
ぎい、と閉じていたはずの船窓が開いたのには二人とも仰天した。それで雨風激しく吹きこんできたならまだ納得いったものの、窓の開きは緩慢で、外でも風雨は籠もったように低い。ならば何故開いた。夜更けの駄目男と哀れな少女の愁嘆場に、雨と風の精がからかい混じりに水を差そうとしたとでも。
　二人はしばし凝結していたが、やがて朔屋は留め金の下ろし方が甘かったのだろうと自分に言い聞かせてまた窓を閉めようとして、
lines.english:
The porthole that should have been shut opened with a creak. Both were startled. Had wind and rain rushed in fiercely, they might have understood. But it opened slowly, and outside the weather sounded low and muffled. Why, then, had it opened? Had spirits of rain and wind come to tease this late-night scene of a useless man and a pitiful girl's sorrow?
For a while they froze. Then Sakuya told himself he must not have lowered the catch properly and reached to close it again.

lines.japanese: 「……今のなに！　今の声、なに！」
lines.english: “…What was that! What was that voice!”

lines.japanese:
朔屋には何も聞こえなかったが、後退るクロの、あまりに真に迫った恐怖の相に偽りとも思えず、そもそもこの娘にそんな小芝居を打つような知性は乏しい。
　だからクロに倣[なら]って耳を澄まして───
lines.japaneseRuby:
朔屋には何も聞こえなかったが、[R後退^あとじさ]るクロの、あまりに真に迫った恐怖の相に偽りとも思えず、そもそもこの娘にそんな小芝居を打つような知性は乏しい。
　だからクロに倣[なら]って耳を澄まして───
lines.english:
Sakuya had heard nothing. But Kuro's retreating terror was too convincing to seem false. In any case, the girl possessed little of the intelligence needed for such a performance.
So, following her example, he listened closely—

lines.japanese:
「え……？　なんか聞こえたか？
　俺には雨風の音しか───」
lines.english:
“Huh…? Did you hear something?
All I hear is wind and rain—”

lines.japanese:
聞こえる───？　否。
　
　
　では聞こえない───？
　
　
　それも、否だった。
lines.english:
Could he hear it? No.
Then he could not hear it?
That, too, was no.

lines.japanese:
船窓に寄り来るは、島から吹き寄せる風。
　雨と波の囁きの中に切れ切れに、幽かに、それなのに言葉と判る音節、入り交じって。
lines.english:
Wind came to the porthole from the island.
Faint, broken among the whispers of rain and waves, sounds were mingled that nevertheless could be recognized as syllables, as words.

lines.japanese:
『我が造りし人を
　　　　　　　拭い去らん
　　　　　　　　人より獣　　　　　　　』
lines.english:
‘Man whom I have made
             I will blot out
                 from man to beast             ’

lines.japanese:
『　　　天空の鳥に至る
　　　　　　滅ぼさん
　　我　　　造りし　　　悔ゆれば　なり』
lines.english:
‘       unto the birds of heaven
               I will destroy
     for I      repent      having made      ’

lines.japanese:
『かくて　　　の後
　　　　　　洪水　　　臨めり
　　大淵の源皆破れ
　　　　　雨　　　注げり
　　　　　　　は　面に漂えり　　　　　』
lines.english:
‘And after       
               the flood       came
     all the fountains of the great deep were broken open
            rain       poured
                 floated upon the surface       ’

lines.japanese:
───夜の雨風の中に言葉が漂うてあった。
　聞かせようとしているのか、ただ語りたいだけか、いずれにしても、怒り、哀しみ、悔やみ、そして───呪う言葉。
lines.english:
Words drifted in the night's wind and rain.
Did they mean to be heard, or merely wish to speak? Either way, words of anger, sorrow, regret—and a curse.

lines.japanese:
風の中に訴えのかのような声は。
　或いはこの世界の記憶であり───
　
　もしかしたら鎮魂の歌なのかも知れないが。
　だとしてもあまりに禍言めいて、朔屋の顔色死人のように青ざめさせ、
lines.japaneseRuby:
風の中に訴えのかのような声は。
　或いはこの世界の記憶であり───
　
　もしかしたら鎮魂の歌なのかも知れないが。
　だとしてもあまりに[R禍言^まがごと]めいて、朔屋の顔色死人のように青ざめさせ、
lines.english:
The voice in the wind, like an appeal—
Perhaps a memory of this world.
Perhaps a song for the repose of the dead.
Even so, it sounded far too much like words of ill omen. Sakuya's face turned pale as a corpse.

lines.japanese:
「……いや、確かに何か、島から。
　こりゃあ、なんだ───うっ？」
lines.english:
“…No, there's definitely something,
from the island. What is this—ugh?”

lines.japanese:
腕に食いこんだ痛みに顔しかめ、振り返ればクロが、震える恐怖の塊だった。かくりと膝を突き、今にも倒れそうな体、支えていたのは朔屋の腕を掴んだ手。彼女自身は意識していなかったろうが、強く強く握りしめた手。クロにしては信じられないほど強い力が、恐怖の程を示していた。
　吹きこむ風から身を避けようと、朔屋の半身に縋[すが]って額を押し当てる、まるで見なければ聞かなければ、世界には自分を脅かす恐怖など存在しないとでも言うかのように。
lines.english:
Pain bit into his arm. Grimacing, he looked back and saw Kuro, a trembling mass of fear. Her knees had buckled; her body was about to fall. What supported her was the hand gripping his arm. Probably without knowing it, she clutched him tightly, tightly. A strength unbelievable in Kuro showed the measure of her terror.
She pressed her forehead against his side, clinging to him to avoid the incoming wind. As if not seeing, not hearing, would mean the world contained nothing that could frighten her.

lines.japanese:
「朔屋さん、クロは怖い。
　ほんとは……来たら、いけなかった？
　朔屋さん、クロを、クロを、助けて」
lines.english:
“Mr. Sakuya, Kuro's scared.
Maybe Kuro… shouldn't have come after all?
Mr. Sakuya, help Kuro. Help Kuro.”

lines.japanese: 夜の船、船員達は寝静まっているけれどもそこかしこに寝息や寝言が密かに響いて、生命の気配はあちこちに聞こえていたのにクロと朔屋はそれらから隔絶されて、ただ二人だけで夜の声の脅威に晒されて、お互いをただ一つの人肌のよすがとして抱き合っていたけれど、風の中から声が完全に消えた頃合いに、クロがようやく漏らした。
lines.english: Night aboard the ship. The sailors slept, but breaths and muttered dreams sounded quietly here and there. Signs of life could be heard everywhere. Yet Kuro and Sakuya were cut off from them, exposed alone to the menace of the night's voice. They held each other as their sole refuge of human warmth. When the voice had completely vanished from the wind, Kuro finally spoke.

lines.japanese:
「あれ……クロ、変。
　まだなんにもなってないのに、
　助けて、なんて」
lines.english:
“Huh… Kuro's strange.
Nothing's happened yet,
and Kuro's asking for help…”

lines.japanese: いったい何にあれほど怯えていたのか、彼女自身理解が及ばぬ、もどかしげな、けれど知ってしまうのも恐ろしいような、そんな微妙な表情で、朔屋の目を見上げ、ころりと小石のように軽く哀しく独りごちたのだった。
lines.english: She herself could not understand what had frightened her so badly. With a delicate expression of frustration, yet fear of knowing too, she looked up into Sakuya's eyes. Her words fell lightly and sadly, like a pebble, spoken to herself.
